answer: The gale debit happens at intake, reef totals the burned amount, and island anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm hence pays the burn once for each alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 2 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. A 75 account operation therefore ties up 27 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
